functions.name: begin
functions.docs:
returns an iterator to the first row (rowwise) or column (colwise) of the nested expression.
\sa end(), cbegin()

functions.name: cbegin
functions.docs: const version of begin()

functions.name: rbegin
functions.docs:
returns a reverse iterator to the last row (rowwise) or column (colwise) of the nested expression.
\sa rend(), crbegin()

functions.name: crbegin
functions.docs: const version of rbegin()

functions.name: end
functions.docs:
returns an iterator to the row (resp. column) following the last row (resp. column) of the nested expression
\sa begin(), cend()

functions.name: cend
functions.docs: const version of end()

functions.name: rend
functions.docs:
returns a reverse iterator to the row (resp. column) before the first row (resp. column) of the nested expression
\sa begin(), cend()

functions.name: crend
functions.docs: const version of rend()

functions.name: redux
functions.docs:
\returns a row or column vector expression of \c *this reduxed by \a func
The template parameter \a BinaryOp is the type of the functor
of the custom redux operator. Note that func must be an associative operator.
\warning the size along the reduction direction must be strictly positive,
otherwise an assertion is triggered.
\sa class VectorwiseOp, DenseBase::colwise(), DenseBase::rowwise()

functions.name: minCoeff
functions.docs:
\returns a row (or column) vector expression of the smallest coefficient
of each column (or row) of the referenced expression.
\warning the size along the reduction direction must be strictly positive,
otherwise an assertion is triggered.
\warning the result is undefined if \c *this contains NaN.
Example: \include PartialRedux_minCoeff.cpp
Output: \verbinclude PartialRedux_minCoeff.out
\sa DenseBase::minCoeff()

functions.name: maxCoeff
functions.docs:
\returns a row (or column) vector expression of the largest coefficient
of each column (or row) of the referenced expression.
\warning the size along the reduction direction must be strictly positive,
otherwise an assertion is triggered.
\warning the result is undefined if \c *this contains NaN.
Example: \include PartialRedux_maxCoeff.cpp
Output: \verbinclude PartialRedux_maxCoeff.out
\sa DenseBase::maxCoeff()

functions.name: squaredNorm
functions.docs:
\returns a row (or column) vector expression of the squared norm
of each column (or row) of the referenced expression.
This is a vector with real entries, even if the original matrix has complex entries.
Example: \include PartialRedux_squaredNorm.cpp
Output: \verbinclude PartialRedux_squaredNorm.out
\sa DenseBase::squaredNorm()

functions.name: norm
functions.docs:
\returns a row (or column) vector expression of the norm
of each column (or row) of the referenced expression.
This is a vector with real entries, even if the original matrix has complex entries.
Example: \include PartialRedux_norm.cpp
Output: \verbinclude PartialRedux_norm.out
\sa DenseBase::norm()

functions.name: lpNorm
functions.docs:
\returns a row (or column) vector expression of the norm
of each column (or row) of the referenced expression.
This is a vector with real entries, even if the original matrix has complex entries.
Example: \include PartialRedux_norm.cpp
Output: \verbinclude PartialRedux_norm.out
\sa DenseBase::norm()

functions.name: blueNorm
functions.docs:
\returns a row (or column) vector expression of the norm
of each column (or row) of the referenced expression, using
Blue's algorithm.
This is a vector with real entries, even if the original matrix has complex entries.
\sa DenseBase::blueNorm()

functions.name: stableNorm
functions.docs:
\returns a row (or column) vector expression of the norm
of each column (or row) of the referenced expression, avoiding
underflow and overflow.
This is a vector with real entries, even if the original matrix has complex entries.
\sa DenseBase::stableNorm()

functions.name: hypotNorm
functions.docs:
\returns a row (or column) vector expression of the norm
of each column (or row) of the referenced expression, avoiding
underflow and overflow using a concatenation of hypot() calls.
This is a vector with real entries, even if the original matrix has complex entries.
\sa DenseBase::hypotNorm()

functions.name: sum
functions.docs:
\returns a row (or column) vector expression of the sum
of each column (or row) of the referenced expression.
Example: \include PartialRedux_sum.cpp
Output: \verbinclude PartialRedux_sum.out
\sa DenseBase::sum()

functions.name: mean
functions.docs:
\returns a row (or column) vector expression of the mean
of each column (or row) of the referenced expression.
\sa DenseBase::mean()

functions.name: all
functions.docs:
\returns a row (or column) vector expression representing
whether \b all coefficients of each respective column (or row) are \c true.
This expression can be assigned to a vector with entries of type \c bool.
\sa DenseBase::all()

functions.name: any
functions.docs:
\returns a row (or column) vector expression representing
whether \b at \b least one coefficient of each respective column (or row) is \c true.
This expression can be assigned to a vector with entries of type \c bool.
\sa DenseBase::any()

functions.name: count
functions.docs:
\returns a row (or column) vector expression representing
the number of \c true coefficients of each respective column (or row).
This expression can be assigned to a vector whose entries have the same type as is used to
index entries of the original matrix; for dense matrices, this is \c std::ptrdiff_t .
Example: \include PartialRedux_count.cpp
Output: \verbinclude PartialRedux_count.out
\sa DenseBase::count()

functions.name: prod
functions.docs:

Example: \include PartialRedux_prod.cpp
Output: \verbinclude PartialRedux_prod.out
\sa DenseBase::prod()

functions.name: reverse
functions.docs:
\returns a matrix expression
where each column (or row) are reversed.
Example: \include Vectorwise_reverse.cpp

\sa DenseBase::reverse()

functions.name: normalized
functions.docs:
\returns an expression where each column (or row) of the referenced matrix are normalized.
The referenced matrix is \b not modified.
\sa MatrixBase::normalized(), normalize()

functions.name: normalize
functions.docs:
Normalize in-place each row or columns of the referenced matrix.
\sa MatrixBase::normalize(), normalized()
